subject: Pilot unitization: examples for per-call vs per-context floors
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jeff Cole <jeff.cole@acmehealth.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot unit accounting — quick examples attached

Hi Jeff — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I've attached a short SOW draft and a sample pilot scope spreadsheet so procurement can see the commercial framing. Two clarifying questions came up from your team about how we meter long-chat sessions versus single-turn calls:

- Do you want us to count billing as "per-request" (charge = tokens used in request/response rounded up to quantum) or as "per-context" (charge aggregates across an active conversation window and charges the max seen in that window)?
- Do you prefer a per-call floor (e.g., minimum 64 tokens billed per API request) or a per-context minimum (e.g., at least 1,000 tokens billed per active conversation per hour)?

Attached spreadsheet has two worked examples: 1) high-frequency short Q&A (many small requests) and 2) long chat session with a 6k token context and streaming output. If you can confirm which framing your procurement team prefers, we can convert the pilot quote into the right billing table and show monthly estimated usage at the proposed discount tiers.

Attachments: pilot_scope.xlsx, SOW_draft.pdf

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Jeff Cole <jeff.cole@acmehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 11:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot unit accounting — quick examples attached

Thanks, Tessa. Procurement is looking at this now and flagged two practical ask items: we need concrete worked math for the long-chat scenario (we run 1k clinicians doing 1–2 hour sessions ~3x/week; sessions average 4k tokens in, 3k tokens out). They want to understand sample invoices under both models.

Also: during pilot we expect low concurrency but long sessions; if we get charged a per-call floor on every streaming packet that'd blow the pilot budget. Can you show the math with a few variants: per-request floor = 128 tokens, per-request quantum = 32 tokens; or per-context floor = 2,000 tokens billed per active conversation per day.

I've attached a sample transcript. Our legal also asked whether a first-month waiver of minimums is possible.

-Jeff

Attachment: acme_sample_transcript.txt
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Pilot unit accounting — quick examples attached

Tessa/Team — drafted some quick back-of-envelope examples for Jeff's use-cases. Notes and assumptions below (open to refinement):

Assumptions:
- Tokenization: we charge per-token; invoice increments in 32-token quanta (round up to nearest 32).
- Per-request floor option: bill max(tokens_request + tokens_response, 128) then round up to nearest 32.
- Per-context floor option: for activeconversation windows we bill the peak observed token footprint once per hour, minimum 2,000 tokens per active conversation per day (helps long sessions).
- Pilot discounting: standard pilot discount table proposed at 15% for <$500k ARR-equivalent, 20% for >$500k (negotiable).

Worked examples (using Jeff's numbers):
1) Long session, non-streaming aggregate (4k in / 3k out): tokens = 7000 -> per-request model (single call) -> billed tokens = max(7000,128) = 7000 -> rounding to nearest 32 = 7024 tokens billed.
2) Streaming + multiple packets: if streaming emits 30 packets of ~100 tokens each (output total 3k), per-packet billing with 128 min -> each packet would bill max(100,128)=128 -> 30 * 128 = 3840 tokens billed (plus input tokens). This is why per-packet floors hurt streaming.
3) Per-context floor approach: treat the conversation as a single active context for the day -> billed tokens = max(peak_context_size, 2000) = max(7000,2000) = 7000 -> rounding to 7024. In this case per-context and per-request are similar for large sessions, but per-context helps when sessions are many short packets with small per-packet outputs.

Recommendation: offer Acme two billing options on the pilot quote so they can choose: A) per-context billing (hourly window) with a 2k/day floor; B) per-request billing with a reduced per-packet floor of 64 tokens for streaming to avoid overbilling pilots. For the pilot, we can waive the first-month floor for both options.

I'm comfortable with a 15% pilot discount and approving a one-month waiver; any larger discount (20%+) should be escalated to RSD and finance.

Sergio
Sr. Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jeff Cole <jeff.cole@acmehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot unit accounting — quick examples attached

Hi Jeff — thanks for the sample transcript and the volume estimate. Sergio's worked examples are attached below; key points: 

- For your long sessions (7k tokens total) both per-request and per-context produce similar billed totals because the session footprint is large. The main difference shows up for streaming/small-packet patterns.
- We will include both billing tables in the pilot quote so procurement can pick which they prefer.
- Pilot commercial concessions we can offer: 1) First-month floor waiver; 2) Pilot discount of 15% applied to usage; 3) Rollover not enabled during pilot but can be discussed for committed term.

If that works, please confirm which billing mode you prefer and we will send an updated SOW + DocuSign link. Also: could you confirm the expected monthly token run-rate after the pilot (ballpark) so finance can size the committed-seat discount if you move to a 12-month commitment?

Links: HubSpot deal RDW-ACME-2027-01, DocuSign SOW (placeholder)

Thanks — Tessa
From: Jeff Cole <jeff.cole@acmehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 09:16:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot unit accounting — quick examples attached

Tessa/Sergio — appreciate the clarity. Procurement prefers the per-context billing for the pilot because of streaming behavior. Counterpoints/asks from their side:

1) Can Redwood waive minimums for the first pilot month (we will be heavy on sessions but need predictable cost).
2) For a 12-month commitment after pilot, Acme asks for a 20% volume discount (they've provided a PO estimate of ~120M tokens/mo post-rollout).
3) Rollovers: they ask that unused pilot-month tokens (if any) roll into the first committed month.

Their procurement contact referenced PO-1423 for internal tracking. If the waiver + 20% are off the table, let us know the nearest compromise.

-Jeff
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Quick internal: approved approach to respond:

- Offer: first-month floor waiver for the pilot (approved).
- Pilot discount: 15% (approved).
- Post-pilot 12-month commitment: authorize negotiation up to 18% discount. Anything >18% requires RSD/Finance sign-off.
- Rollover: we can offer one-time rollover of unused pilot tokens into month 1 of a paid commitment (legal to write specific language).

Vanessa, please loop Legal to prepare a SOW with the per-context pilot billing table, the first-month waiver, and the note about rollover into month 1 of a commitment. Tessa — go ahead and send the SOW/DocuSign with the revised terms and flag the 20% ask as counter to our 18% ceiling without additional approvals.
